name: index_constituent_spread_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: When a Nifty50 constituent deviates significantly from the index's intraday move (stock return vs beta-adjusted index return), it tends to converge. This is because index-level buying/selling (via ETFs and index futures) creates uniform pressure on all constituents, but execution lags cause some stocks to respond slower. The slow responders eventually catch up. Edge persists because computing real-time beta-adjusted residuals for 50 stocks requires continuous recalculation infrastructure.
stock_filter: all Nifty 50 constituents, ranked by beta-adjusted residual

exit.trailing_stop: move stop to breakeven when z-score crosses ±1.0

risk.position_sizing: beta_adjusted — position size inversely proportional to beta

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: skip if stock volume < 50% of 20-bar avg
filters.event_filter: skip stock on results day; skip on expiry day
other_filters: skip stocks that just got added/removed from the index (beta unstable)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — structural but ETF arbitrageurs are getting faster

weaknesses: This is a single-leg trade (not hedged with index) so you have directional risk if index moves
Beta estimation error on rolling 20-day window can cause false residual signals
On stock-specific news days, the residual is driven by genuine information, not mean-reverting flow
prior_art: Index vs constituent spread trading — used by index arbitrage desks globally
notes: Consider adding index futures hedge (short Nifty futures when long constituent) for purer alpha.
